physics_goals.note: Quote is the abstract as served on the APS page (TeX markup).
physics_goals.quote: We report the analysis of the spatial energy distribution of data for ${e}^{+}{e}^{\ensuremath{-}}\ensuremath{\rightarrow}\mathrm{hadrons}$ obtained with the MARK-J detector at PETRA.
physics_goals.value: Analyse the spatial energy distribution of e+e- annihilation into hadrons and test QCD (three-jet structure from quark-antiquark pairs with hard gluons)

summary.plain: One of the four original detectors at DESY's PETRA collider, built by a collaboration of European, American and Chinese institutes led by Samuel Ting. Its 1979 analysis of the energy flow in e+e- collisions showed three-jet events and supported the existence of the gluon.
summary.technical: MARK J at PETRA: collaboration led by S. Ting; institutes named on the 1979 PRL: III. Physikalisches Institut (TH Aachen), DESY, MIT Laboratory for Nuclear Science, NIKHEF-H Amsterdam, and the Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Science, Peking. Data-taking January 1979 to 3 November 1986; the 1979 three-jet analysis used the 'oblateness' variable.
